# pulse_client (Resource)

A client: one tool's own NATS identity, with permissions built from its grants. A client without grants can connect but do nothing.

The `.creds` file is returned only when the client is created or its credentials are rotated. It is kept in state (sensitive) and never re-read, so protect the state. Change `creds_version` to rotate the credentials: the old ones stop working and their connections are closed.

Grant changes apply to live connections. Destroying the resource revokes the client permanently and removes its record. A client revoked outside Terraform is removed from state and planned for re-creation (under the same name). Import with the client ID or name; the credentials are then unknown until rotated.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A home-automation bot that publishes door events, replays them with its own durable consumer and stores large
# payloads in the shared blob store.
resource "pulse_client" "door_bot" {
  name        = "door-bot"
  description = "Door sensors"
  tags        = ["home"]

  grants = [
    { action = "publish", subject = "evt.home.door.>" },
    { action = "durable", subject = "evt.home.>", name = "doors" },
    { action = "blobs" },
  ]
}

# Hand the .creds file to the tool, e.g. as a file on its host.
resource "local_sensitive_file" "door_bot_creds" {
  content         = pulse_client.door_bot.creds
  filename        = "${path.module}/door-bot.creds"
  file_permission = "0600"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique name: lowercase letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, at most 64.

### Optional

- `creds_version` (String) Arbitrary value; changing it (including setting it for the first time, e.g. after an import) rotates the credentials and stores the new `.creds`.
- `description` (String) Description.
- `expires_in_days` (Number) Lifetime of the credentials in days (1-3650, default 365). Changing it rotates the credentials, which then expire this many days after the rotation.
- `grants` (Attributes Set) What the client may do. `publish`, `request` and `reply` take a `subject`; `subscribe` takes a `subject` and optionally a `stream`; `durable` takes a `subject`, a `name` and optionally a `stream`; `blobs` takes nothing and allows the shared blob store. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--grants))
- `tags` (Set of String) Free-form tags shown in the dashboard.

### Read-Only

- `creds` (String, Sensitive) The `.creds` file (JWT and seed). Only known after create or rotation; never re-read.
- `expires_at` (String) When the current credentials expire (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) Client ID.
- `status` (String) `active`, or `expired` when the credentials have expired (rotate them).
- `user_key` (String) The client's current NATS user public key (changes on rotation).

<a id="nestedatt--grants"></a>
### Nested Schema for `grants`

Required:

- `action` (String) One of `publish`, `subscribe`, `request`, `reply`, `durable` or `blobs`.

Optional:

- `name` (String) Durable consumer name for `durable` grants: the client may use the consumer `<client id>_<name>` (see `pulse_consumer`).
- `stream` (String) Stream for `subscribe` and `durable` grants. Default `EVENTS`.
- `subject` (String) Subject or wildcard pattern (`*` one token, `>` the rest), for example `evt.home.>`. Required for every action except `blobs`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By ID or by name. The credentials are unknown after an import until they are rotated (set creds_version).
terraform import pulse_client.door_bot door-bot
```
